measurement.theUniversalIsTheFalsifiableForm_andItIs: This artifact does something better than its peers: it states the closure claim as a testable universal rather than leaving it implicit. That is exactly the sentence the corpus praises elsewhere. Tested, it fails — /sliceStanding is named by neither the roster nor by succession metadata, and it changed in three places. The universal quantifies over PATHS ('Every path … names'), and no path named /sliceStanding is named anywhere.
measurement.theChangesAreDescribedButThePathIsNotNam: honestyRepairsFromV1's fifth entry describes the content of these edits — 'CLAUDE-V1-ADV-1/2/3: D-096 is an owner grant not a deferral; no sealed-row claim; keychain unexercised in first slice'. So the work is disclosed. But describing a finding is not naming a path, and the universal is written in terms of paths. A reviewer bounding the diff by the roster would not look in /sliceStanding.
measurement.whatMakesItAvoidable: The roster is otherwise precise to a sub-path — it names '/recordedInputs/governingSources (append file 02)' rather than the whole object, and flags '/reviewGuidance (append)'. The drafter was tracking paths at fine grain and still omitted the object carrying three of the five repairs.

The miss is in the direction that costs the guarantee: under-inclusive, not over-inclusive. And the escaping object is not incidental — it holds three of the five claimed repairs.

verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 2 SHOULD-FIX, 3 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. REJECT.
verdictStatement: The repair that mattered is done, and done better than I asked. My v1 finding was that the third broker prohibition was minted — unsourced, and phrased as a containment guarantee that file 03 specifically withholds. v2 drops it, keeps only the two elements that trace to law, and replaces it with a routing statement naming two carriers. I checked both rather than accepting the citation, and both are real: file 02 lines 190-191 say components 'must not … bypass host brokers', and DR-105 owns enforced-confinement versus trusted-code consent. The clause then closes by citing the very confinement-honesty sentence it previously contradicted. That is the opposite of the failure I found in an adjacent row this week, where a repair routed an obligation to an artifact that existed nowhere; here the targets were verified before being trusted. The rest holds up under the same pressure: carries byte-exact against live at the current HEAD, the row anchor unique, all four re-measurement digests exact at the HEAD the block names, no API or algorithm or path invented, no owner grant, no numbers, and the TM material routed to DR-011 with its freeze-block scoping preserved rather than widened. My own v1 verdict is recorded accurately down to the digest. What fails is bookkeeping, twice, in the same object. The artifact upgrades its closure claim into an explicit falsifiable universal — every path not named is unchanged from v1 — which is the better form and therefore the higher standard; tested, three paths escape it, all in /sliceStanding, which is exactly where three of the five claimed repairs live. And within that object the successor adopted the vocabulary rule my ADV-2 asked for while leaving the sentence that breaks it byte-identical, so 'Absence of a sealed DR-108' now sits two keys above a rule stating that sealed vocabulary does not apply to the register row — recorded, meanwhile, as folded, under a notFoldedThisSuccessor that is explicitly empty. Neither defect touches the architecture and neither is a blocker. Both are one-line fixes: add /sliceStanding to the roster, and change one word in firstSlice.

coordinatorNote: REJECT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-108 stays OPEN at file 08 line 290; I did not touch file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, marked nothing SATISFIED, invented no keychain/file/broker API, and minted no D-096 (A) grant. Six things to weigh. First, direction of travel is strongly positive: the one substantive defect in v1 is properly fixed, and fixed by routing to carriers I verified exist rather than by re-wording. Both remaining findings are clerical and neither touches the architecture. Second, both repairs are one line: add /sliceStanding to the roster string, and change 'sealed' to 'SATISFIED' in sliceStanding.firstSlice. On my measurement a v3 doing only those two things carries zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. Third, on S-2 I want the coordinator to see my reasoning rather than just the grade: the underlying wording is trivial and its proposition is true either way, but notFoldedThisSuccessor is empty and honestyRepairsFromV1 reports the item repaired, while the target string is byte-identical to v1 — reporting a repair whose target did not move is the one thing that field must not do, and that, not the vocabulary, is why I did not leave it as an advisory. Fourth, S-1 is worth noting as a pattern rather than a one-off: this is the second successor I have reviewed this week whose closed roster omitted the object holding its own repairs, and in both cases the roster was otherwise precise to sub-path granularity. Fifth, the independence limitation: I have never read either Codex verdict in this series, so v2's record of CODEX-SSCV1-S1/A1/A2 is digest-matched but content-unverified by me; I judged those three on their merits and all three hold, but convergence between the lanes on the containment finding is genuine rather than an artefact of one reviewer reading the other. Sixth, a process note: the review prompt pins HEAD at 2d5f15b while actual HEAD is 8daa2e6 (D-110). Immaterial here — file 08, file 03 and file 02 are all byte-unchanged, and D-110 touches DR-125's successor candidate without disturbing this artifact's DR-125 reservation — but prompt HEAD pins continue to age within the review window.
